parts.markdown:
Use our free Wisconsin paycheck calculator to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Wisconsin income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Wisconsin's employer withholding calculation uses income-dependent deductions and employee withholding exemptions. Understanding these adjustments is important when estimating your salary after taxes.

Whether you work in Milwaukee, Madison, Green Bay, Kenosha or another Wisconsin community, this calculator can help you compare employment opportunities and manage your monthly expenses.

## How to Use the Wisconsin Paycheck Calculator

Choose annual salary or hourly wages and select the pay schedule shown on your pay stub. Hourly employees can enter their regular hours and qualifying overtime.

Enter the federal and Wisconsin income tax withheld for that pay period. Use the full withholding amounts, including any additional withholding.



Include employee retirement contributions, eligible health premiums and other deductions from the same pay period. Enter each deduction once.

Enter prior year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching a Social Security or Additional Medicare threshold.


## Wisconsin Payroll Taxes in 2026

Visit the [Wisconsin Department of Revenue](https://www.revenue.wi.gov/) for official information about income taxation and employer withholding.

## Wisconsin Income Tax Rates in 2026

Wisconsin uses progressive individual income tax rates.

The applicable 2026 annual income tax rates are 3.50%, 4.40%, 5.30% and 7.65%.

However, Wisconsin's authorized alternate employer withholding calculation uses a different percentage schedule.

This distinction matters because payroll withholding represents advance payments toward your annual tax liability rather than a complete annual tax return calculation.

Employers should use the applicable withholding tables or authorized alternate method from Publication W-166.

Read the official Wisconsin Withholding Tax Guide for complete instructions.

## Wisconsin Employer Withholding Percentage Schedule

The authorized alternate method applies the following rates after subtracting applicable withholding deductions and exemptions.

These thresholds are specific to the alternate employer withholding calculation.

They should not be confused with Wisconsin's ordinary annual income tax brackets.

## Wisconsin Income-Dependent Withholding Deductions

Wisconsin's alternate employer withholding method incorporates deductions that gradually decrease as annualized earnings increase.

For single employees:
- The maximum ordinary withholding deduction is $6,702.
- The deduction decreases by 12% of earnings above $17,780.
- The deduction becomes zero at $73,630.
For married employees:
- The maximum ordinary withholding deduction is $9,461.
- The deduction decreases by 20% of earnings above $25,727.
- The deduction becomes zero at $73,032.
These amounts affect payroll withholding rather than directly representing the standard deductions available on an annual Wisconsin tax return.

## Understanding Wisconsin Form WT-4

Wisconsin employees use Form WT-4 to communicate state withholding information to their employers.

Each qualifying withholding exemption has an annual value of $400 under the alternate calculation method.

The modern federal Form W-4 cannot be used as a substitute for Wisconsin's state withholding certificate.

Employees may also qualify for a separate employee withholding agreement through Form WT-4A.

Obtain the applicable certificates from the Wisconsin withholding tax forms directory.

Review your withholding elections when starting a new job or experiencing changes in household income.

## How to Calculate Wisconsin Income Tax Withholding

Consider a single employee earning $65,000 annually and claiming one ordinary withholding exemption.

First, calculate the applicable withholding deduction.

Annual earnings exceeding $17,780:

$65,000 − $17,780 = $47,220.

Deduction reduction:

$47,220 × 12% = $5,666.40.

Remaining deduction:

$6,702 − $5,666.40 = $1,035.60.

Subtract the remaining deduction and one $400 withholding exemption:

$65,000 − $1,035.60 − $400 = $63,564.40.

Apply the applicable withholding bracket:

$1,045.04 + (($63,564.40 − $25,520) × 5.30%).

Annualized withholding equals approximately $3,061.39.

For 26 biweekly paychecks, estimated Wisconsin withholding is $117.75.

This example uses the authorized alternate method. The official wage-bracket tables may produce slightly different results.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Wisconsin Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable earnings, payment frequency, filing status and Form W-4 information.

Employees with multiple jobs, other income or eligible tax credits may have different deductions.

Employers follow the procedures in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered wages up to $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings.

Additional Medicare withholding of 0.9% generally applies to covered earnings exceeding the employer's $200,000 annual withholding threshold.

Visit [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and the Social Security Administration contribution and benefit base for official payroll requirements.

## Wisconsin Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose an employee earns $27 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$27 × 40 = $1,080.

Overtime earnings:

$27 × 1.5 × 6 = $243.

Total gross earnings: $1,323.

Federal and Wisconsin income taxes and ordinary payroll contributions are then calculated using the relevant taxable wage amounts.

Review the Wisconsin Department of Revenue for employer withholding guidance. Use the [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) to compare compensation and the [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) to estimate a savings cushion.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Which form controls Wisconsin payroll withholding?

Employers use Form WT-4 and the applicable Wisconsin withholding instructions. Enter the amount actually withheld from your pay stub in this calculator.

### Is Wisconsin withholding my final state income tax?

Withholding is a payment toward your annual tax. Compare your actual withholding and tax liability when you file.

### Why might my Wisconsin paycheck differ from this estimate?

Differences in taxable wages, allowances, employer rounding and benefit deductions affect take-home pay. Use amounts from the same pay period.
